summary.en: Use **can** and **could** for ability, permission and requests: _I **can** swim_, _**Could** I borrow your pen?_ Use **be able to** where _can_ has no form: after other verbs, in the future and in the perfect tenses. For one successful action in the past, use **was able to**, not _could_.
summary.es: Can y could sirven para capacidad, permiso y peticiones. Cuando can no tiene la forma que necesitas (futuro, presente perfecto, infinitivo), usa be able to. Para un logro concreto en el pasado, was able to, no could.

form: **be able to** + infinitive: _He **was able to** finish early._
Questions and requests: **Can / Could / May** + subject + infinitive
Negative: **can't / cannot / couldn't / wasn't able to**

uses.text: **General ability**: _She **can** speak three languages._ _I **could** swim when I was five._
**One successful action in the past**: _The firefighters **were able to** save the building._ (Not _could_ in an affirmative sentence.)

note.en: In negatives, couldn't is fine: They couldn't save it.

uses.text: **Ability in other tenses**: _I **haven't been able to** call her all week._ _You'll **be able to** park here soon._
**Asking for permission**: _**Can** I use your phone?_ _**Could** I leave early today?_ _**May** I come in?_ (the most formal)
**Giving or refusing permission**: _You **can** park outside._ _You **can't** smoke in here._
**Polite requests**: _**Could** you send me the report?_ _**Would** you mind closing the door?_

mistakes.wrong: Yesterday I could finish the report before lunch.
mistakes.right: Yesterday I was able to finish the report before lunch.

why.en: For one particular success in the past, use was able to. Could describes general ability.
why.es: Un logro concreto en pasado: was able to. Could es para capacidad general.

mistakes.wrong: She can to play the guitar.

why.en: Modal verbs are followed by the infinitive without to.
why.es: Tras un modal no se usa to.

mistakes.wrong: I will can come to the meeting.
mistakes.right: I will be able to come to the meeting.

why.en: Can has no infinitive, so it cannot follow will.
why.es: Can no tiene infinitivo: «podré» es will be able to.

mistakes.wrong: Do you can help me with this form?
mistakes.right: Can you help me with this form?

why.en: Modals make questions by inversion, without do.
why.es: Los modales no llevan do en preguntas.

examples.en: My grandfather can still repair almost any clock.
When I was a child, I could run for hours without getting tired.
examples.es: De niño podía correr durante horas sin cansarme.

examples.en: After a long search, the police were able to find the missing dog.
I couldn't open the window because the handle was broken.
I haven't been able to sleep properly since the building work started.
examples.es: No he podido dormir bien desde que empezaron las obras.

examples.en: Will you be able to pick up the parcels on Friday?
Could I borrow your charger for a few minutes?
May I ask who is calling, please?
Visitors can use the car park, but they can't stay overnight.

practice.prompt: Last night the engineers ___ repair the fault in under an hour.

explanation.en: One particular success in the past needs was/were able to.

practice.prompt: I'm sorry, I ___ come to your party next week. I'll be abroad.

explanation.en: Can't + infinitive without to; no do with modals.

practice.prompt: Excuse me, ___ I use the toilet, please?

explanation.en: May I is a polite way to ask for permission.

practice.prompt: With a new bike, you ___ cycle to work in twenty minutes.

explanation.en: Can has no infinitive, so use will be able to.
